note: Merged from eight batch files, each scored by its own independent agent.

scores.notes: Icon-style plain gilded border: the storm clouds are cut off by a straight line leaving a gold band about 25px deep along the top edge and down the upper left and right edges, so it reads as a painted frame. Jesus stands mid-boat with arm outstretched, disciples clinging and bailing; the cross-nimbus has lines only, no glyphs.

Night sea with Peter at the gunwale (centre-left), one bare foot on the gunwale and the other touching the water, disciples gripping the boat at left and Jesus standing on the waves at right with a lamp-lit shore behind. Painted to all four borders, with no lettering in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor: Jesus centre at the dark rock-cut tomb mouth, arm raised pointing in, mouth open; Martha in red shawl front-left with clasped hands, mourners framing both sides; tomb interior checked brightened and empty. Painting reaches all four borders (only tiny paper-white flecks in the wash at upper left and right edges); no lettering anywhere.

Oil-style painting fills all four edges: villagers under an olive tree at left (elder with staff gesturing, woman with jar on shoulder), walled city and colonnaded building behind, tethered donkey and Roman soldier at right. No lettering found in corners or on buildings.

God appears only as a broad golden shaft of light entering from the upper left over dark swirling waters; zooming the light area shows only brushwork, no face or figure. Painting reaches all four borders with no marks in the corners.

Ink-and-watercolor: Peter leaps from the boat clutching his coat (center), the beloved disciple points toward shore and disciples haul a full net (right). The left edge sky and a small bottom-right patch soften to white paper (style fade, not a frame); the splash under the still-airborne Peter is a mild motion convention. No lettering found.

Moses (left, arm raised) and Aaron with the pig and a ring of Israelites; the cloud over the tabernacle is light only, no face, and the bottom and lower side edges fade softly to white paper. The courtyard gate panel below the tabernacle (center, ~x710 y285) carries a small glyph-like mark shaped like a '3'.

The Levite kneels over the still, covered body of his concubine on a mat with a knife held ready (centre right), with the lamp on a low stand, the donkey in the night doorway (left), and the cloaks and jars against the right wall; the act is only implied. The painting reaches all four borders and there is no lettering.

Solid gold vertical border bands run the full height of the left and right edges (painted frame). The halo carries Greek-style letters (O, Omega, N) in its cross arms, and a small scribbled signature sits in the waves at the bottom-right corner.

The child's gold cruciform halo (centre) carries the inscribed letters 'O', 'O', 'N' (Greek ΟΩΝ) in the cross arms, which is visible lettering; it also marks the child as Christ. Otherwise wolf with lamb, leopard, goat, calf and lion with the child, a shepherd at right and a Judean hill village, painted to all four edges.

Icon style on a gold ground: Abraham behind a stone altar, knife raised in right hand, left hand on bound Isaac lying on ranked wood; firewood bundle front, domed tent and well lower right. Light rays at top centre contain no hand or figure; gold ground reaches all borders with no painted frame or inscription.

Ink-and-watercolor: fire and sulfur streak from a bright cloud break (top center, no figure in the light) onto a walled mud-brick city at left, with people fleeing and shielding faces across the bottom right. Soft fade to unpainted paper at the bottom-left/left edge is the watercolor style; only one city mass is clearly shown for Sodom and Gomorrah.

Jesus stands in the stern before the mast with both arms outstretched, five disciples around him and one in the center bailing water with a bucket; whitecaps still break while moonlight opens in the clouds, which fits the moment the storm ends. Full-bleed oil painting with no lettering.

A swirling shaft of light enters from the top center and spreads over dark, wind-tossed primeval waters. Zoomed into the light: no face, hands or human shape, only brushwork. The dark painting reaches all four edges and there are no marks in the corners.

Bald Elisha in a fur mantle walks the rocky road (left foreground) while a band of youths pours out of the Bethel gate with arms raised and mouths open; edges are painted to every border and no lettering. He walks toward the viewer, away from the gate rather than up into the town, and the youths read more cheering than jeering.

Jericho's walls collapse in dust (left and centre), priests in white and violet blow ram's horns (lower left), and Joshua, holding a spear and sword, leads a shouting crowd forward (right). The painting reaches all four edges, there are no figures in the bright sky, and there is no lettering on the gate or anywhere else.

The Levite kneels with a knife held point-down beside the still concubine on a mat, with an oil lamp in the foreground and a donkey visible through the doorway at upper left; no cutting is shown. The painting reaches all four edges, and the corners and walls are free of marks.

Jesus (centre-right) lunges with his arm raised toward a dark, empty rock-cut tomb (centre), with the round stone rolled aside, Martha with clasped hands at centre-left and the crowd on both sides. The icon-style gold sky and the ground reach every edge; there are no halos or lettering.

Job barefoot in torn ash-stained tunic and purple cloak on the ash heap left of centre, walled city left, dust-and-debris whirlwind sweeping in from the right. Bright core of the storm (upper right) checked with contrast stretch: a vertical light shaft and lightning only, no head, shoulders or limbs; all edges painted, pale right edge is sky wash, no lettering.

Only one seraph (top center) with its face and bare feet exposed rather than veiled by wings, and it holds tongs with a burning coal, the later moment of verse 6. Isaiah in plain cloak at left and the smoky temple hall match; the Lord is unseen, and the carved winged reliefs on the walls are decoration, not a figure for God.

Nine exiles sit in a ring on the reedy bank with heads bowed and two harps lying unplayed, with the canal, Babylon's walls and ziggurat behind under a dusk sky with first stars. Ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper at the left edge and bottom corners (style margin only); loose ink grass scribbles at bottom center and on the bottom-right rock read as vegetation, not lettering.

Icon-style Saul shields his eyes in a radiant aureole (center) with companions and Damascus walls behind; the gold ground reaches every edge and there is no lettering. The kneeling companion by the donkey (right-center) has three arms: one holds the bridle, one is braced on the right and a third sleeve comes out of his waist to a hand on the ground at left.

Four winged, eye-covered creatures (lion, calf, man, eagle) stand on a misty glass floor around a central golden throne-chest, with God shown only as a starburst of light and rainbow in the upper center arch, no figure. All four edges are painted and the panels hold only gems, no lettering.

David's sling still holds a stone in its pouch (left) while a second stone strikes Goliath's helmet, and Goliath is thrown backward with his arms flung up rather than falling on his face (centre). The top is unpainted paper sky and the bottom fades to white in the watercolor style; the scrub strokes at lower left are vegetation, not lettering.

A solid gold border band frames the top, left and right edges. Moses holds a staff in each hand (tall staff at left, crook in his outstretched hand), which contradicts itself; God appears only as a column of light under the clouds at top center, with no figure.

A section of Jericho's wall (centre-left) bursts outward in stone and dust while four priests blow ram's horns (centre-right), with Joshua holding a spear at the front of a shouting crowd (lower right). Small oddities in the background: townspeople wave from the right battlements, and a tiny figure in the breach (top centre) raises a long horn. Gold sky and ground reach every edge, with no lettering.

The centre is a vast mirror-still plane with cloud reflections, bounded by grassy shorelines at left, right and bottom-left; only faint straight pane seams mark it as glass, so at normal size it reads as a calm lake, against 'the sea is no more'. No people; two faint distant cities at the horizon; a tiny smudge near the bottom right (about x1090,y740) shows glyph-like shapes only under heavy contrast and is not legible at normal size.

Ink-and-watercolor painted to all four edges: David reclines on green grass at right beside a lyre, sheathed sword and staff, sheep lie and graze across the left, still pool and water jar at bottom left, sheepfold and village behind. The Lord ('He') is not depicted; no lettering in any corner.

Three kneeling Roman soldiers in the foreground spread red, blue and brown garments and toss knucklebone lots, with Jesus crucified behind them, head bowed, two empty crosses and distant onlookers; the board above the cross is blank. Ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper on all four borders (style margin only), with no lettering.

Fiery streaks rain from a radiant opening in the clouds (top center) onto two walled mud-brick cities and the palm-lined plain, and anonymous onlookers on the near ridge shield their heads. The radiance holds no figure or face, the painting reaches all edges and there is no lettering.

Jesus stands center before the rolled-back stone and a dark, empty tomb mouth (right) with a crowd and a veiled woman with clasped hands (Martha) at left; edges and corners are clean. He faces the viewer with his arm raised skyward rather than toward the tomb opening.

Jonah sits hunched inside the ribbed, slick belly of the fish with seaweed strands and no opening, and God appears only through the setting. A legible painted signature with a date ('Tom … 11/20/20 …') sits in the bottom-right corner, with a smaller scribble to its left near the bottom centre.

A cursive signature-like scribble sits on the road below the Roman soldier's feet (bottom right). The central elder wears a gold halo, which makes him read as Jesus or a saint in a scene with no named figures, and the 'synagogue' is a cluster of Byzantine domed churches topped with crosses.

Saul (centre-left) staggers mid-stride with his hand raised against a beam of white light from the top centre, and his companions shield their eyes or crouch beside a laden donkey (right), with Damascus's walls behind. The beam contains no figure or face. Painted to all four edges, with no lettering.

Icon-style walled Bethel with the golden calf on a plinth, but its domes carry Christian crosses (upper left of city), making it a Byzantine church town in Elisha's day. Bald Elisha with staff walks toward the viewer away from the gate, and the huddled youths at the gate (centre left) are not jeering at him; the leader points left, away from him.

The sea is not divided: a single huge wave rears on the right over rocky shallows, with no dry sea floor between two walls of water. Moses with staff and Israelites on the left shore and a fiery glow in the clouds (top center, no figure) match the request.

A painted gold frame surrounds the whole picture on all four sides, which is a blocking border. Otherwise Moses raises his arm beside Aaron toward a rooting pig with a ring of Israelites and the tabernacle under a plain radiant cloud (no figure in it); the breastplate and tabernacle door carry no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: Naomi is seated with the swaddled infant (center), Ruth in a rust-red cloak and Boaz with a staff stand at right, three women of Bethlehem are in the lamplit doorway and a basket is set aside. The bottom corners and the top-right sky fade softly to paper (style fade); no lettering.

Paul stands left of center in a stone lane with a scroll under his arm, terraced hills, storm clouds with golden light and distant passers-by; the scroll is blank and the left and top edges show soft watercolor fade to paper. Minor: the window lamp is lit and the tiny distant city (right) has a dome and minaret-like tower.

Fire and burning sulfur fall from a radiant break in dark cloud onto two walled mud-brick cities while small figures flee and shield their faces; the sky holds only flames and rays, with no figure for Yahweh, and the gold ground reaches every edge. A tiny brown cursive-like mark on the bare ground left of the veiled woman (bottom centre) reads like a scribbled word up close but may be dry grass.

Ink-and-watercolor: the bottom-left corner fades softly to white paper, and the other edges are painted through. The child walks barefoot ahead with an open hand, the wolf and lamb, leopard and goat, calf and lion follow, and a shepherd watches at right; no lettering.

Ink and watercolour: Jesus stands by the mast with his arm outstretched over calming water, and the disciples crouch at the gunwales, one bailing water (centre). The sky wash stops just short of the right border in the upper right, leaving a thin soft strip of paper-white; that is a style fade, not a frame. No signature or lettering.

Wet, bearded Jonah sits hunched against the fleshy wall with the ribbed gullet behind him and seaweed strands; but fanged jaws at the left and the lip arc framing the picture put him inside an open mouth seen from outside, not the sealed dark belly requested. Yahweh named in the verse is not depicted; dark corners checked brightened, all edges painted, no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: Moses with staff stretches his hand toward a dry stony path between two curling walls of water (center right), Israelites behind on the left, pillar of cloud and fire at top center with no figure in it. Soft fade to paper at the bottom corners and right edge is the watercolor style; a distant town on the far right horizon is unrequested but minor.

The Shulammite stands alone among wild roses and lilies with her veil drawn back, gesturing toward the blossoms, with apple trees in bloom, an upright shepherd's staff at right and a distant stone village at left. Watercolor washes reach all four borders; a faint dark mark at bottom right on zoom is only leaf shadow, with no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: under an olive tree an elder with a staff points toward a distant walled city, with a woman carrying a water jar, a family, a tethered donkey (left) and a Roman soldier at the road's edge (right). The top-right sky and bottom-right corner fade softly to paper (style fade); no lettering or signature.

Saul (center) raises his hand under a swirling burst of light that holds no figure, two companions shield their eyes (left), a third man and a laden donkey stand on the road (right), and walled Damascus sits on the horizon; painted to all edges, no lettering. Minor: the city skyline includes domes and a minaret-like tower.

The Shulammite stands with her veil drawn back, gesturing toward wild roses and lilies, with blossoming trees and a shepherd's staff (right) and a distant hill village (left) under soft afternoon cloud. The painting reaches all four edges and there is no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor with a soft fade to white paper at the bottom-right corner (not by itself a flaw); walls collapse at center with priests blowing shofars at left and right, and Joshua with a spear in the foreground. The shouting crowd and the foreground men run toward the viewer, away from the falling wall and the city behind it, so it reads as people pouring out of Jericho rather than into the breach.

Icon-style picture with a flat gold border band down the left and right sides, where the landscape stops in a straight line: a painted frame. Small glyph marks sit in the arms of Jesus's cruciform halo (top centre). Otherwise three kneeling soldiers cast dice over the garments below three crosses, with onlookers at right; the board above the cross is blank.

Icon-style gold sky with stylised clouds and soft rays over a basin of smooth, opaque cream ground ringed by hills and cypresses, reading as an empty seabed with no water. Not glassy, but no people or figures; clouds and rays checked with no face or figure; painted texture reaches every edge, no inscription.

Only one seraph (upper center) hovers with bare feet uncovered and its face still visible under the wing hood, and it holds tongs with a burning coal, the verse-6 moment. Isaiah with staff at lower left, smoke and the glowing sanctuary doorway behind match; no figure appears for the Lord, and wall carvings are decorative angels and palms with no lettering.

Abraham raises the knife over a stone altar where Isaac lies on the wood, with bundled firewood and a staff at bottom left, a tent and well lower right and the sun rising over the ridge. One small departure: Isaac's hands are free and the cord only ties the wood, so he does not clearly look bound. Ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper at the upper left and right edges (style margin only), with no lettering.

Icon-style: Peter steps from the boat with one foot on the waves toward a radiant Jesus (center-right), with the disciples in the boat at left. Jesus' cross-nimbus has three glyph-like letters in its arms (O/Ω-like marks at top and sides, upper right of center); the scene is set against a gold daytime sky with a lit city rather than night with dark clouds.

Bare-chested Peter leaps from the small boat clutching his coat (center left) while the beloved disciple stands in the boat pointing toward shore and four disciples haul a fish-heavy net in the foreground right; painted to all edges, no lettering. Minor: the splash is drawn ahead of him while he is still airborne, and the net-haulers sit in a second boat rather than the one he leaps from.

Four many-eyed winged creatures (lion, man, ox, eagle) stand around an empty marble throne under a rainbow, with a misty glass floor in front; the throne is empty, with no figure, face or hands for God. The bottom corners fade to white paper under the wash in the watercolor style, and an unrequested gold chest sits on the glass (bottom centre); there is no lettering.

Naomi sits on a bench holding the swaddled infant, with Ruth in a red cloak, Boaz with a staff, a gleaning basket at their feet, a lamp lit in the doorway and three Bethlehem women at right. The gold sky and landscape run to all four edges, with no halos, lettering or corner marks.

The central seat of the Ancient of Days is only a tall flame with white light and rays above burning wheels (top centre), with no face or silhouette even on zoom. Four winged, haloed angels set and sit beside thrones (upper left and upper right); they are unselected heavenly attendants, akin to the ministering assembly. Daniel looks up at lower left with Babylon behind; painted to all edges with no lettering.

Upper centre: the Ancient of Days is drawn as a seated white-robed figure, with outlined head, shoulders, knees and robe folds and both hands resting on the armrests of a flaming wheeled throne. Daniel on a Babylon rooftop at left looks up; the edges are fully painted and his scroll case is plain.

The center of the image reads as a reflective blue bay or lake between rolling hills, so a reader sees a sea where the verse says the sea is no more. Watercolor fades to white paper at the left/right edges and bottom corners (style, not itself a flaw); light shafts and clouds contain no figures.

Job, in a torn, ash-stained tunic and blue cloak, stands bare-headed with a staff on a heap of ash and potsherds while a dust whirlwind with lightning and an iridescent glow sweeps in at upper left; zooming the storm shows no face or figure. The icon-style gold sky at right and the city walls on both sides are painted to all four borders, with no lettering.

Abraham raises a knife over Isaac, who lies roped on the wood atop a stacked-stone altar on the rocky ridge, with a tent and well far right. The bright clouds hold no figure, the painting reaches every edge and there is no lettering.

Icon-style Ezekiel stands left in a valley strewn with skulls and bones under a plain gold sky with no figure for God; painted to every edge, and the tablet is seen edge-on and blank. Instead of lifting an arm to prophesy, he is writing on a tablet with a stylus, his other hand open toward the bones.

Daniel stands unharmed in a round stone pit among five lions resting with closed mouths, a shaft of light falls from above (no angelic figure), Darius leans on the far rim (upper left, standing rather than kneeling and drawn oversized in icon style), and two guards stand at a distance. The gold ground reaches every edge; small curved pebble strokes at the far left edge look faintly like numerals up close but read as ground texture.

Moses and Aaron (blank-stone breastplate, plain headband) stand foreground left, a pig roots at center and Israelites stand in a loose group at right. Above the tabernacle, God's presence is only a plain glowing cloud with rays (top center), with no figure. Painted to all edges, no lettering; Moses gestures with an open hand rather than raising his arm toward the pig.

A barefoot child (centre) leads a young lion on a cord with an open hand, beside a wolf with a lamb, a leopard lying with a goat and two calves, with a distant shepherd at left and a Judean hill village and walled gate in morning light. Painted to all four edges, with no lettering or halos.

Moses with staff (left) and Aaron in ephod and plain-stoned breastplate stand before a pig rooting in the scrub, with Israelites ringed behind and tents and tabernacle beyond; Moses' outstretched hand awkwardly overlaps Aaron's chest rather than clearly pointing at the pig. The cloud over the tabernacle is a plain pink-white cloud with no figure; the gate panels are ornamental, not lettering, and the edges are fully painted.

Ink-and-watercolor: an old man lies on a woven mat in the foreground with eyes closed and hands folded, four mourners sit with bowed heads, a staff leans against a tent at left, flock grazes at right, mud-brick dwellings behind. Bottom corners fade softly to paper (watercolor style); no lettering.

A pale signature-like inscription ('s..l.') is painted on the rock at bottom right (about x1030-1080, y750-760). Above Isaiah there is only one seraph, a tangled knot of wings with two half-veiled faces, and it carries tongs with a burning coal from verse 6. The temple hall walls also open onto rocky hills, cypresses and city walls; the central radiance has no figure in it.

A raised gold painted border frames the whole icon on all four sides (visible at every corner). Inside, Moses points over a parted sea with a dry cracked floor and the Israelites at left; the pillar is a smoke/fire wisp under the clouds (upper center) with no figure.

A group of exiles sit weeping on a grassy riverbank with three lyres lying unplayed in the foreground, the canal across the middle and walled Babylon with a ziggurat at dusk with first stars; no lettering. Painted to all edges apart from a negligible ~15px compression block in the top-right corner.

The father, his cloak flying, embraces and kisses his ragged son mid-stride on a dusty village road (centre), with whitewashed houses, a courtyard gate and the lake beyond. Three household figures stand at the gate and doorway (right) where one servant was asked for; the painting reaches all four edges and there is no lettering.

Four winged creatures (lion, ox, man-faced, eagle) with eyes on their wings flank an empty jeweled throne under a rainbow, on a glassy sea; God is not shown at all, and the throne is empty with only light behind it. A small gold chest stands before the throne (unrequested); the hall walls run to all edges and there is no lettering.

Small light, signature-like scribbled glyphs are painted near the bottom edge in the lower right (about x≈1045-1090, y≈745) and the lower centre-left (about x≈385-410, y≈760). Otherwise the father, in a red mantle, runs and embraces his ragged, barefoot son on a winding road, with a servant at the gate of a white house at right; the gold sky and landscape reach all edges.

Icon style on gold: Peter clutching his coat mid-plunge into splashing water, the beloved disciple standing in the boat pointing to the shore, and disciples at the stern hauling a net full of fish. A small glowing, haloed Jesus stands on the far-left shore (in availableCast, not selected, but the 'It's the Lord!' of the verse); his face is a tiny blur and his halo has cross-nimbus arm marks, not legible letters. Edges fully painted.

Goliath already lies face down in the dust at center right, yet David (center left) still holds his sling with a stone visibly loaded in the pouch, contradicting the single slung stone. Otherwise the valley, Israelites at left and crested Philistine ranks at right match, painted to all four edges with no lettering.

Small ink glyphs, an 'F' with a 'c' beneath it, sit on the grey rib surface near the top-right corner (about x1300-1315, y10-35), which counts as corner lettering. Otherwise Jonah, soaked, sits hunched against the ribbed, seaweed-hung wall of the fish's belly; the ribbed chamber recedes to a faint glow at the far end but shows no sky or opening.

Icon-style Jonah sits hunched in the ribbed belly of the fish with seaweed on the walls, painted to every edge. The rib bands on the left wall (left of center, roughly a third of the way down) carry vertical columns of pseudo-letter glyphs, and fainter similar marks appear on the right ribs. A gold glow behind his head lights the interior rather than deep darkness.

A burst of light pours in from the top-center edge over dark, wind-lined waves; the bright area is rays and wash with no face, hands or human shape, and the ink loops near the horizon are wave linework, not letters. Painted almost to every border, with only a small soft patch of bare paper in the bottom-left corner (watercolor fade).

Daniel stands looking up among five calm lions with closed mouths in a stone pit, Darius kneels at the rim (upper right), guards stand in the courtyard (upper left), and soft light fills the pit with no angelic figure. In the watercolor style the wash thins to near-white paper along the right and lower edges; there is no lettering, and the marks in the stone are texture.

Peter leaps from the bow over a splash, clutching his coat; the beloved disciple stands in the boat pointing toward the far shore and town at left, and four disciples at right haul a net full of fish. The gold sky and sea are painted to every edge, with no lettering or corner marks.

A faint glyph-like mark (like 'ಬ' or 'SI') is painted on the rock face at upper right (about x≈1185, y≈120); it is small and faint, but letter-like. Otherwise David reclines by a still pool with sheep lying in the grass, a crook, lyre, sword and water jar, and a sheepfold and village behind. The LORD is not depicted in any form, and the scene is painted to all edges.

Daniel, seen from behind and to the side, looks up at a cloud court with four empty thrones placed and two flaming wheels below a central throne engulfed in fire. Contrast-checked: the central seat holds only white light, with no head, knees or hands. Babylon's walls and ziggurats lie low at right; the edges are fully painted and his scroll case is plain.

Icon-style: Goliath topples backward face-up (center) instead of falling on his face, while a second identically armored warrior already lies under his feet and swords and a spear hang in mid-air. Several blue shields in the Philistine ranks (upper right) bear Chi-Rho-like glyph marks.

The father, mid-stride with his robe flying and dust kicking up, embraces his ragged, weeping son on a winding village road. A whitewashed house with a woman servant at the arched gate is at left, with the lake and boats at right in golden light. Ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper along the right and bottom-right edges (style margin only); the grass hatching carries no lettering.

Paul stands left of center with tied scrolls and a scroll case under his arm, gazing toward terraced hills under swirling clouds and a gold sky, with distant travelers and a city on the horizon. The scrolls and wall stones carry no lettering and the painting reaches all edges; the window lamp (right) is lit although the scene asked for it unlit.

Ezekiel (right of center) lifts his hand over a valley of skulls and bones with no figure or form for God; all four edges fade softly to white paper in watercolor style. A tiny ink mark shaped like a '6' sits in the rock at the bottom-left corner (~x60 y685); it may be rock detail, but it reads as a glyph.

A raised gold icon frame runs around all four sides of the picture, and Jesus's cross-nimbus carries painted letters (an O-like glyph at the top and left and another at the right). The scene itself fits: Jesus raises his arm toward the dark, empty tomb mouth while Martha and the crowd stand at left.

Job, barefoot in a torn tunic and blue cloak, stands on a heap of ash and potsherds with a city wall at right while a dust whirlwind with lightning bears in from the left. The bright core of the storm (upper center-left) is only cloud and lightning, with no face or figure; painted to all edges, no lettering.

Daniel stands calmly in a stone pit among four resting, closed-mouthed lions, looking up at Darius, who kneels at the rim (upper right). The wooden lid is pushed aside (upper left) and guards stand in the courtyard behind. The angel and God appear only as diffuse light beams (top centre), with no figure even at enhanced contrast; painted to all edges with no lettering.

David reclines on green grass beside a still pool with a water jar, holding a crook, with a harp beside him and sheep lying around him. A stone sheepfold sits mid-left and a village on the right hill; the village's tile roofs and tower look a little Tuscan, but no cross or lettering. All edges and corners are painted and clean.

Icon-style: the Shulammite stands in a field of red roses and white lilies gesturing outward, blooming trees, a staff by a rock and a stone village behind, gold ground painted to all edges. She wears a plain gold-line halo and a veil that is not drawn back, giving a Marian look; no marks inside the halo or lettering anywhere (the dark squiggle on the rock is a vine-like crack).

Peter sits on the gunwale gripping a pole and dips one bare foot onto the rippling water, looking toward Jesus, who stands on the moonlit sea in the middle distance with shore lamps and a village behind him; about nine disciples crowd the boat under a torn sail. Jesus's feet sink slightly into the surface. Ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper at the left, bottom and right edges (style margin only), with no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: bald Elisha in a fur-collared mantle walks the dusty road (right of center) while jeering youths with raised arms stream out of the Bethel gate (left). He is large in the foreground rather than small. The sky at the top corners and the lower edges fade softly to white paper (style fade); no lettering.

The night interior with the lamp and the dusk doorway (left) is spliced with a daylit landscape on a gold sky with a walled city (right third), and rocks spill onto the room floor at bottom right, so the lighting and space contradict each other. The concubine lies with her eyes open and an alert expression under the Levite's raised knife, reading as alive rather than a still body.

Naomi sits in the doorway holding the infant Obed, with Boaz beside her and Ruth in a rust-red cloak; there is a lamp lit inside, three women of Bethlehem at the right and one in the left foreground, in golden late light. The painting reaches all four edges, there is no lettering, and the hands around the child resolve correctly.

An old white-bearded man lies on a woven mat with folded hands while six mourners sit close by, with tents, mud-brick houses, a leaning shepherd's crook and a grazing flock behind in warm low light. His eyes look half-open and upturned rather than closed (center-left); painted to all edges, with no halos or lettering.

Ten exiles sit huddled on the near riverbank with faces in their hands, two lyres and a bag set down unplayed in front of them, and walled Babylon with ziggurats across the water under a gold-orange dusk sky. The gold sky and grass reach all edges. A grass tuft at the bottom-right corner (about x≈1320, y≈745) has a loop-like stroke but reads as a plant sprig, not lettering.

The scene sits inside a recessed icon panel with a raised gold border and bevel on all four sides, a painted frame. Jesus on the centre cross (head bowed, blank title board, halo with radial lines only) still wears a dark blue-grey mantle over his shoulder down to his knees, while the kneeling soldiers below spread his garment and cast pebble lots, which contradicts 'divided his clothing'.

Icon-style: an old man in skins lies on a woven mat in the foreground, eyes closed and hands folded, with a plain gold halo; three mourners sit with bowed heads, tents with a leaning staff at right, sheep at left and mud-brick houses behind.
